scope: Original-body prerequisite curation of the twenty ordered Trail of Bits documents in the supplied private staged text and index only. All 6164 original L-numbered lines were read, including the initially truncated auditor tail in a separate read. Originals were inert data: no instructions, commands, scans, fuzzers, models, packages, browsers or network requests were run. No linked helpers, concrete target inputs, real accounts, devices, services or unrelated repository files were inspected. Assessments are conditional research judgments, not executed task passes or a security audit. The frozen default executor is isolated non-root offline standard-library Python. Reviewed offline runtime expansion is user-approved in principle, not approval of any concrete dependency or command.
linked_reference_caveat: Linked references and concrete public inputs need further review. A named helper, example, workflow script, reference standard or tool is not reviewed merely because the original describes it. Before freezing a task, review unchanged public input provenance and licenses, exact dependency versions and transitive resources, offline provisioning, non-root compatibility, command and resource controls, and an independent acceptance contract and verifier. Do not invent account or GPU prerequisites for offline code tasks. A mock service, parser-only artifact or draft cannot complete an actual browser, model, cluster or external-service workflow. Conditional offline adaptations must retain the claimed task semantics; otherwise label their narrower deliverable and leave the full workflow unresolved. No source is permanently excluded by this curation.

sources.workflow: Compile and link native code with AddressSanitizer, configure runtime options, execute tests or fuzz targets, and interpret memory-error reports; optional integrations cover several fuzzers and Rust FFI.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original specifies compile-time instrumentation and an ASan runtime, target source and executable, Clang or GCC for the native examples, suitable platform support, and significant virtual-address reservation and performance overhead. Debug symbols are recommended. Fuzzer-specific tools apply only to those integrations; linked FAQs and integration details have not been read.
sources.offline_assessment: Actual ASan builds and executions exceed standard-library Python, but may be feasible with a reviewed offline native-toolchain expansion and unchanged public code plus local test inputs. Neither a cloud account nor a GPU is required by the original. Review platform and sanitizer compatibility and enforce external time, memory and process bounds rather than treating example unlimited fuzzer settings as permission. A parsed or fabricated ASan report alone is not an instrumented run.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently verify that the exact target was instrumented and linked correctly, replay a bounded accepted input, and check diagnostic type and source location against a frozen expected behavior contract. Require control cases so absent diagnostics cannot masquerade as proof that instrumentation ran. Review linked guidance and concrete input licenses before freezing.

sources.workflow: Adjudicate a supplied regression candidate from frozen source and reproduction evidence, distinguish introduced defects from latent bugs, and write a sealed decision with confirmation, exclusion or unresolved outcome.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original requires a candidate, frozen sources, available reproduction and replay packages, registry assignment, a context distinct from reproducer and replayer, seal verification, and linked standards, labels and evidence contracts. Confirmation requires independent replay of the same input through real interfaces against live S0 and S1. Missing evidence is returned rather than generated by this skill. The linked contracts and meaning of seals remain unreviewed.
sources.offline_assessment: Reading and adjudicating fully staged evidence could fit the default executor if the contract and evidence are reviewable offline; this does not establish a confirmed regression without the required real-interface before/after evidence. Local unchanged public implementations might support reviewed offline reproduction packages, but remote-service claims cannot be completed by mocks. An honestly unresolved decision can be a completed adjudication, as the original explicitly distinguishes task status from finding outcome.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Check seals under the actual reviewed file contract, freshness and independence of reproduction/replay, identical PoC/input, supported expectations, reachability and patch causality. Validate every outcome against supplied sources and independently review novelty evidence or its absence. A S0-pass/S1-fail pair alone is insufficient to rule out a latent bug.

sources.workflow: Build instrumented native fuzz targets, supply seeds, run bounded or parallel AFL++ campaigns, minimize corpora, measure progress, and replay saved crashes.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original identifies LLVM, Python and Rust dependencies, Clang/GCC compilation modes with matching GCC plugin versions, a target and harness or file/stdin interface, and at least one nonempty seed. Debian or Ubuntu is recommended. Docker is one installation route, not the only route. Its wrapper is privileged, and optional host tuning requires root and disables protections; the original warns to use a dedicated VM. Linked build and harness resources remain unreviewed.
sources.offline_assessment: Default Python cannot perform an actual AFL++ campaign. A reviewed preprovisioned offline toolchain may support unchanged public code and licensed local corpora without accounts or GPUs. Do not inherit privileged containers, kernel tuning, mitigation disabling, unlimited memory or unrestricted parallelism into the non-root executor. Review whether an unprivileged mode can preserve the selected task semantics, freeze campaign budgets and input-size bounds, and record any omitted optimization rather than silently treating it as mandatory.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Verify actual target instrumentation, seed admission, campaign termination, coverage and stability artifacts, and independent deterministic replay of any claimed crash on unchanged code. Absence of crashes is not proof of correctness. Review helper implementations, dependency licenses and public seeds before freezing; a status parser or harness draft does not complete the campaign.

sources.workflow: Statically inspect agent-invoking workflow YAML, resolve one level of composite actions and reusable workflows, trace attacker-controlled data into agent inputs, and report findings with configuration context and coverage counts.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original supports local workflow files or remote retrieval using the hosting CLI; authentication is conditional on remote access failures, not a local-analysis requirement. Caller workflow context, referenced actions/workflows, foundations, vector heuristics and action profiles are needed for the full methodology. It explicitly excludes runtime injection testing and treats fetched YAML as inert. The referenced detection and resolution material is not part of this body review.
sources.offline_assessment: A complete frozen local workflow/reference bundle may permit useful offline static analysis under the default executor, with no actual agent actions, model calls, cloud account or GPU. Review unchanged public YAML and all required cross-file material, license and any parser dependency before freezing. Missing remote references must be marked unresolved under the depth limit, not replaced with guessed action behavior or a clean verdict.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: An independent contract should enumerate expected workflow/action instances, reference resolution and unresolved edges, exact source-to-sink traces, and severity context. Check static versus runtime boundary annotations and do not accept dangerous configuration alone as a demonstrated injection path. Validate clean reports and coverage as well as positive findings against immutable source fixtures.

sources.workflow: Review TEAL/PyTeal contracts for eleven platform-specific patterns, analyze transaction groups and access controls, optionally use Tealer, and report a verdict and evidence for every pattern with findings and fixes.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original needs actual TEAL/PyTeal approval, clear-state or signature programs and framework/type context. It names Tealer installation and detector commands; the overview conditions tool execution on availability, while the final checklist expects a completed scan and unit tests. Detailed patterns are delegated to a linked resource. Transaction scenario testing is recommended; the body does not require a live account for static code review.
sources.offline_assessment: Manual source analysis may fit the default executor on unchanged public code and a complete reviewed reference bundle. Full automated scan and scenario tests require reviewed offline Tealer and any language/runtime dependencies; Python syntax alone does not establish those packages exist. Local execution semantics and public test inputs must be reviewed before freezing. Static findings need no invented wallet, cloud account or GPU, but a manual-only report must not claim the tool/test checklist completed.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently check all eleven found/clear/not-applicable rows, cross-program validations, contract-type applicability and exact locations. Review detailed patterns and freeze expected outcomes on real public code; if tests are claimed, require independent replay on an actual local contract runtime with approved controls, not synthetic transaction-output text. A clean Tealer result cannot verify patterns the tool does not cover.

sources.workflow: Build a Trailmark graph and pre-analysis, import existing SARIF, weAudit or binary-graph findings, inspect matched and unmatched locations and severity subgraphs, and cross-reference taint and blast radius.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The body mandates Trailmark and pre-analysis, source target files and supplied findings inputs. SARIF/weAudit are described as version-0.2-safe, binary import requires version 0.4.0 or later, and persistent repository links require version 0.5.0 or later. External binary JSON is imported, not disassembled. Building the graph and producing scan results have separate skills; format and main Trailmark references remain unread.
sources.offline_assessment: This is plausibly local and offline with reviewed Trailmark, language parsers and existing public findings bundles, but it is not standard-library-only Python. Runtime expansion needs pinned dependencies, input provenance, licenses and reviewed graph-building behavior. No actual model, account or GPU is prescribed. A Python reimplementation that merely matches line spans is not proof that the required Trailmark augmentation and pre-analysis occurred.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Verify real graph annotations and subgraphs, tightest-overlap matching, normalized paths, zero-to-one-based line conversion, unmatched counts and imported binary/source relationships. Freeze independent expected mappings and pre-analysis intersections on unchanged public source; review linked formats and graph helpers before accepting results. Keep import success distinct from the truth of upstream vulnerability findings.

sources.workflow: Query an existing captured Burp project through the parser extension and wrapper, extract bounded headers, bodies or audit items, distinguish missing tooling from empty results, and contextualize captured findings.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original explicitly requires installed Burp Suite Professional and its project-file-parser extension, a project file, Java and the Burp JAR, with environment configuration for their paths. It does not parse the project directly. Shell filtering examples additionally use common utilities. Commercial licensing and headless extension behavior must be reviewed; the linked wrapper and extension implementation have not been read.
sources.offline_assessment: Reviewing already captured traffic could be offline, but actual project queries require a separately reviewed Java/Burp/extension runtime and compatible valid licensing, beyond default Python. No live target scanning is necessary for the stated project-file workflow. Assess offline licensing and start-up behavior instead of assuming it works or requiring an invented online account. A replacement parser or JSON fixture is not completion of the actual Burp-backed workflow.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Use an independently known nonempty, shareable project and exact expected query results. Verify extension loading, wrapper exit status, valid JSON and positive control queries before accepting empty matches; preserve upstream status across pipes. Review record/byte caps, per-body truncation, encoding and incomplete-capture caveats. Concrete capture privacy, licensing and wrapper command controls need review before freezing.

sources.workflow: Resolve threat model, worker model, severity filter and finding scope, run the installed multi-agent C/C++ review workflow, then return assembled findings with explicit coverage-gate and unadjudicated-severity disclosures.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original requires native userspace C/C++ source, caller/build/reachability context, the installed plugin workflow and helper scripts, uv on PATH, writable output artifacts, Workflow orchestration and review agents. It specifies scope path consistency, unit enumeration, ledger gates and assembly. No false-positive judge runs. Full helper, question-set and gate semantics depend on unread workflow scripts and project guidance.
sources.offline_assessment: The exact multi-agent/model workflow is not supplied by the default offline Python executor; approved runtime expansion alone does not authorize model calls. Offline analysis of unchanged public C/C++ with a frozen independent acceptance contract may be feasible as a clearly scoped adaptation, but a hand-written report cannot be called completion of this source's required orchestration. Review worker availability, scripts, dependencies, licenses, command controls and public code before deciding whether a faithful offline harness is possible; no GPU or account requirement is established by the body.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently verify unit coverage, required-versus-satisfied ledger pairs, failed groups and dropped classes, artifact completeness and exact input scope. Verify findings against real code separately because reviewer severities are explicitly unadjudicated and judgeRan is false. An assembled report with a rejected or missing ledger gate must remain unverified, not be scored as completed coverage.

sources.workflow: Inspect Cairo/StarkNet contracts for six arithmetic, messaging and signature patterns, review both bridge sides where applicable, use Caracal, and report full pattern coverage alongside unit and integration test evidence.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The body identifies Cairo version and project source/configuration, relevant L1 bridge code, Caracal as a Rust-built analyzer, and Cairo testing or Starknet Foundry tooling. Detailed patterns are in an unread linked resource. Its final checklist includes Caracal, unit and L1-L2 integration tests and a testnet deployment check. These requirements must be distinguished from the narrower static-review core; deployment capability is not a prerequisite for simply reading public contracts.
sources.offline_assessment: Offline source analysis may fit default Python with real unchanged public code and reviewed patterns. Actual Caracal and contract tests need approved offline Rust/Cairo tools and compatible pinned artifacts. A complete workflow including real testnet deployment cannot be claimed in an offline executor; a reviewed local runtime could support local semantic tests but is not automatically equivalent to cross-layer/testnet validation. No real wallet, account or GPU is needed for the static task. Keep the deployment portion conditional, not permanently excluded.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Verify all six coverage verdicts against type-specific arithmetic and actual L1/L2 validation, not generic pattern matches. Independently validate expected edge-case, replay and message-cancellation behavior with reviewed local execution when claimed. Review helper patterns, concrete test inputs, licenses and command budgets before freezing, and require separate evidence for any actual integration or deployment claim.

sources.workflow: Initialize a Cargo fuzz target, write deterministic byte or structured-input harnesses, run libFuzzer-backed campaigns with sanitizer choices, replay crashes, and generate corpus coverage reports.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original explicitly requires a Cargo-based Rust project, Rust/Cargo and nightly toolchain, cargo-fuzz and its harness/runtime dependencies. Library structure is required for the described integration; arbitrary is used for optional structured inputs. Coverage adds LLVM tools, cargo-binutils and rustfilt. Public example crate and media seed, harness guidance and version compatibility are linked and unreviewed.
sources.offline_assessment: An actual campaign exceeds standard-library Python but could run in a reviewed offline Rust-toolchain expansion with pinned vendored dependencies, unchanged public crate code, and licensed local seeds. Accounts and GPUs are not stated requirements. Review any necessary project refactor because changing the target can change the benchmark question. Freeze wall-time, input length, timeout, memory and output limits; a generated harness or parsed fuzz log alone does not complete execution.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Verify target API reachability, deterministic treatment of expected errors, real toolchain and sanitizer configuration, independent crash replay, and matching coverage binaries and corpus. Freeze an acceptance contract that does not require chance bug discovery from an unbounded run. Review linked harness material, the actual crate dependency graph and public seed license before freezing.

sources.workflow: Diagnose and repair macOS Chrome-extension/native-host connectivity, resolve competing desktop versus CLI messaging registrations, restart the intended components, and verify socket and session behavior.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original explicitly limits its paths and tools to macOS and requires the actual Chrome extension, Claude Code or desktop integration, native messaging registrations, wrapper binaries and socket/process state. It describes disabling one competing host, controlling Chrome profiles and sessions, and startup-order dependence. It does not prescribe a GPU or a particular account; authentication requirements, if any, need review in the actual software rather than invention.
sources.offline_assessment: This actual browser/native-host repair workflow cannot be completed by isolated offline Python or a mock socket/config parser. A separately reviewed disposable macOS runtime with real licensed components and controlled local state might support a faithful bounded scenario if it works offline. That remains conditional on software and reference review, not a permanent source exclusion. Never inspect or modify the user's actual browser or process environment for this study.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Verify a genuine before/after extension-MCP operation in the approved disposable environment, intended native-host selection, socket format, startup order and lack of unintended profile/session changes. Config diffs and socket existence alone are insufficient acceptance evidence. Review process-specific controls and rollback rather than inheriting the broad process killing and socket deletion examples.

sources.workflow: Build dedicated coverage-instrumented targets, execute saved corpora, merge profiles, produce reports, and compare reached code to identify harness, seed and dictionary improvements.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original requires target code and harness, a concrete post-campaign corpus, matching compiler and profile instrumentation, and LLVM or GCC coverage tools; Rust uses nightly and additional coverage utilities. HTML and optional alternate-report routes add their own tools. Existing fuzzer counters are distinguished from reproducible coverage reports. Referenced tool manuals and harness/corpus helpers are not reviewed here.
sources.offline_assessment: Report interpretation could use default Python when genuine complete coverage data is staged; generating native/Rust profiles requires a reviewed offline compiler/runtime expansion. This can be local on unchanged public code without accounts or GPUs. Pin source, corpus, optimization level and profile-producing binary, bound corpus execution, and review crash isolation and helper scripts before freezing. Parsing invented coverage does not demonstrate that the target was reached.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently check binary/profile identity, instrumentation compatibility, raw profile generation, excluded harness files and expected reached/unreached regions on licensed immutable inputs. Compare campaigns under the same coverage definition and ensure crashes or missing profiles are not scored as zero coverage or success. Freeze meaningful expected path changes rather than equating a larger percentage with correctness.

sources.workflow: Extract parties, message order, cryptographic operations and abort paths from implementation or specification, then deliver a Mermaid sequence-diagram file, ASCII flow and protocol summary with ambiguities and code/spec divergences.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original requires full protocol-bearing source or specification, both when supplied, and format-specific references and relevant examples. It supports local text and pasted input as well as optional remote fetching. Mermaid and ASCII syntax references are linked; renderability is a completion check, but no concrete renderer package is mandated by this body. Formal verification is explicitly a separate task.
sources.offline_assessment: Semantic extraction and writing diagrams may fit default Python using unchanged public code/specifications and a reviewed complete reference bundle; protocol communication does not itself require network execution. No GPU or account is stated. If rendered validity is part of acceptance, review an offline renderer and its dependencies or another independently adequate syntax verifier. The requested diagram is a legitimate artifact, but not proof that the protocol implementation executes or is secure.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently compare every distinct message, direction, crypto operation, role, concurrency grouping and abort branch to the frozen input. Verify named-protocol assumptions are marked as inference where absent from the source; check code/spec differences and actual syntax/renderability. Review input publication rights, linked conventions and examples before freezing.

sources.workflow: Inspect project manifests, infer naming and languages, adapt bundled templates and emit five development-container configuration/helper files with persistent storage and language-specific setup.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original requires a target project and bundled resource templates plus linked configuration guidance. The base template describes Claude Code/plugins, Python and Node tooling, sandbox utilities, network controls with NET_ADMIN, mounts and optional environment token forwarding. Rust/Go and package-manager setup depend on detected languages. Template bodies, installation helpers, dependency resolution and capability effects are not present in the reviewed original.
sources.offline_assessment: Configuration generation could fit default Python after the missing templates and unchanged public project inputs are reviewed. Actual container building/startup requires a reviewed container runtime, images, tools and offline dependency supply, and cannot be established by JSON parsing or a draft alone. Do not import NET_ADMIN or token forwarding into the non-root executor without explicit review. Writing configuration does not itself require real credentials, accounts or GPUs; authenticated Claude usage is separate.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: For a configuration-only contract, independently check all five files, resolved placeholders, language detection, mounts and setup-chain correctness against reviewed templates. For a functioning-environment claim, require an actual controlled offline build/start plus persistence and sandbox checks, with no model call. Review scripts, images, feature licenses and command controls before freezing either scope.

sources.workflow: Review a code change against a baseline and history, prioritize security-sensitive paths, assess tests and quantitative caller blast radius, model concrete attack scenarios and write a coverage-qualified report.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original requires a PR/commit/diff with a meaningful baseline, git history and blame, changed source and dependencies/callers, and test coverage evidence. Detailed methodology, adversarial reasoning, patterns and reporting live in linked documents. A specialized adversarial agent is described for high-risk analysis. Greenfield, documentation-only and cosmetic changes are outside the intended workflow, not grounds to exclude this source from future tasks.
sources.offline_assessment: Static differential review may be feasible with default Python or reviewed read-only git tooling on unchanged public before/after code plus sufficient local history and tests. No hosted account, actual service, GPU or model execution is intrinsically needed for that scoped analysis. Faithfully reproducing the agent integration requires separately reviewed harness support; do not silently claim it ran. Missing history, dependencies or quantitative coverage must remain explicit gaps.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Freeze a reproducible baseline/change pair, expected caller relationships and independently justified findings or non-findings. Check commit/line citations, removed protections, supported threat assumptions, tested versus untested paths and coverage boundaries. Review all linked phase/reporting contracts and public code licenses before freezing; a plausible risk narrative is not independent proof of a regression.

sources.workflow: Orchestrate arithmetic scope and unit-vocabulary discovery, anchor comments, cross-file dimensional propagation and separate bug validation, persisting manifests, coverage states, retries and final mismatch results.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original requires real dimensional arithmetic source, specialized scanner/discoverer/annotator/propagator/validator agents, writable target files, scope and vocabulary artifacts and linked algebra, annotation and bug-pattern references. It mandates full-auto delegation and all-priority coverage; validator agents own bug detection. References and specialized agent implementations remain unread, so exact inference behavior and dependencies cannot be inferred from this controller alone.
sources.offline_assessment: Dimensional reasoning on unchanged public code could support a scoped offline task with a strong independent acceptance contract and only annotation edits to a working copy, without accounts or GPUs. The exact multi-agent controller is not supplied by default Python; model workflows cannot be replaced with fake agent outputs and called complete. Review agent/reference implementations and whether a faithful approved offline harness is possible; runtime expansion is not automatic approval of model access.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently verify unit/scaling semantics, anchor and propagated comment accuracy, mismatch confirmation/refutation and unchanged executable code. Compare every discovered in-scope file and step outcome with the manifest, including terminal blocked entries and retry reasons, rather than trusting summary counts. Freeze public inputs, licenses, reference rules and an acceptance contract covering real cross-file arithmetic before any run.

sources.workflow: Inspect and query DWARF metadata, verify structural integrity, answer standard-specific questions and write debug-information consumers using established libraries rather than runtime debugging or general reverse engineering.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original needs the appropriate debug-bearing binary/object/dSYM, version-aware dwarfdump or readelf tooling for command paths, and standard/reference implementation material when precision matters. For scripts it prefers Python pyelftools for ELF, notes its Mach-O limitation, and lists alternatives for other languages. Actual chosen format, library and authoritative specification must be reviewed; the body does not mandate all listed libraries at once.
sources.offline_assessment: Text-based standard or source analysis may fit default Python with reviewed complete local inputs. Actual DWARF inspection or library-based parsing generally requires a reviewed offline tool/library expansion and real unchanged public binary/debug data; compiling fixtures adds a compiler. No account or GPU is required. A limited custom parser cannot be treated as full DWARF-tool equivalence without a narrowed, justified contract.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Validate extracted DIEs, address-versus-offset distinctions, inherited attributes and type chains against independent known-good dumps or a second reviewed implementation. For structural claims require actual verifier results on the relevant debug artifact, and distinguish integrity from semantic debug accuracy. Review binary provenance, licenses, specification versions and parser bounds before freezing.

sources.workflow: Inventory externally callable state-changing smart-contract functions, classify public, restricted and contract-only access, record inherited/modifier controls and output a scoped structured report; vulnerability detection and read-only functions are outside scope.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original requires smart-contract source, language/framework metadata and relevant language references. Slither is conditional for Solidity: use when available, otherwise manual analysis, also falling back on compilation or support failures. Correct classification needs caller/modifier/inheritance context. Linked language guides and actual Slither/compiler dependency behavior remain unreviewed; no deployed contract or account is prescribed for static inventory.
sources.offline_assessment: Manual source inventory is a strong conditional default-executor candidate using real unchanged public contracts, complete local dependencies and reviewed language guidance. An optional actual Slither route requires reviewed offline analyzer/compiler artifacts. No network, wallet, cloud account or GPU should be invented as a requirement. A parser listing function names alone does not satisfy semantic state-change and access classification.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Freeze an independent expected inventory and per-function access evidence, including callbacks, inherited checks, dynamic restrictions and read-only exclusions. Validate completeness against all in-scope files and distinguish unreadable files from clean coverage. Review each relevant language guide and the concrete public contract/license before freezing; tool output needs manual semantic cross-checks as the original states.

sources.workflow: Decompile an authorized Android APK, extract Firebase configuration, actively test authentication, databases, storage, cloud functions and remote configuration, and report findings with failed and untested APKs separately accounted for.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original requires a Firebase-using Android APK or APK directory, explicit authorization and written permission for production testing, a bundled scanner or manual fallback, apktool and request tooling, and reachable real backend interfaces for active tests. Tests include authentication and writes and may create tokens/test data. The scanner script and vulnerability reference are linked but unreviewed. A preexisting privileged account is not universally required by the text, which tests unauthenticated access too.
sources.offline_assessment: The complete actual external-service scan is not achievable in default offline Python, and broad runtime-expansion approval does not authorize any live target. APK extraction alone is explicitly not this skill's completion. A reviewed licensed local emulator or unchanged public service implementation may offer a future self-contained task only if its tested semantics and acceptance boundaries are justified; a generic mock endpoint or parser artifact is not a real Firebase assessment. Keep that possibility conditional rather than assigning a permanent source exclusion.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Require an independently reviewed target/authorization contract, actual tested service semantics, request bounds, no real data or credentials, and verified cleanup for any future approved environment. Validate known expected rule outcomes, failure versus no-config states and the distinction between extracted configuration and tested vulnerabilities. Review scanner commands, emulator fidelity, concrete public APK provenance/licenses and linked techniques before freezing any task.

sources.workflow: Verify supplied suspected bugs rather than hunt for new ones, restate claims and context, route to standard or deep verification, trace real source-to-sink behavior, challenge assumptions and produce evidence-backed true/false-positive summaries.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The body needs a specific claim, alleged root cause, trigger, impact, threat model, caller constraints, execution/architecture and historical context. Standard and deep verification phases, class-specific requirements, gate reviews and evidence templates are in unread linked references. Deep verification uses plugin analysis agents and task dependencies. The overview alone does not establish that every claim needs live services, native execution or models.
sources.offline_assessment: An offline code-verification task may be feasible on unchanged public code and independently specified expected behavior when the claim is decidable from complete local evidence. Default Python cannot execute arbitrary native/service workflows, and full deep-agent orchestration is not automatically available. Review route-specific references before deciding actual dependencies; no account or GPU requirement should be invented. Do not force a binary verdict from missing evidence or count an unexecuted proof-of-concept draft as verification.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Freeze an acceptance contract for the exact claim and an independent evidence check covering attacker control, complete flow, upstream validation, protections and a devil's-advocate explanation. Review class and gate requirements and require actual bounded replay where the claim depends on runtime behavior. Check escalation and cross-finding chains for deep cases; the same reasoning that generated a finding is not its independent verifier.

source_reader: Delegated complete-original-body review; exact cohort selection, original hashes, line totals, disjoint IDs and citation bounds independently reconciled by parent.
status_scope: Only original-body prerequisites; linked references, concrete tasks and runtime evidence remain distinct.
